quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign mean?

options.text: It warns of hazards ahead.
It alerts drivers to school zones.
It alerts drivers to recreation areas.
It alerts drivers to food and gas locations.

questions.correctAnswerText: It warns of hazards ahead.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers about hazards. They are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: Why should you stay alert around motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?

options.text: They are hard to see in traffic.
They follow different traffic laws.
They always have the right-of-way.
They don't have rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are hard to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians are smaller and harder to spot than cars. They may also move faster and have less noticeable lights. Always watch for them to prevent crashes.

questions.question: How can you avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Turn your head to look over your shoulder before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn before turning or changing lanes.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to look over your shoulder before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you are moving. Don't rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: What should you do when you hear a fire engine siren behind you?

options.text: Slow down until it passes.
Turn on your flashers.
Pull to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, move to the side of the road and stop.

questions.question: What is the default speed limit on city and town streets?

options.text: 15 mph
25 mph
30 mph
40 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: 25 mph
questions.explanation: Unless a sign shows a different speed limit, the speed limit in cities and towns is 25 mph.

questions.question: What should you do when it starts to rain?

options.text: Drive faster than other traffic.
Drive at the posted speed limit.
Slow down.
Drive close behind the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when it rains. Turn on your headlights so others can see you. If rain is very heavy and you can't see well, pull to the shoulder and stop until it clears.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: Go through if no other cars are coming.
Keep going—you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights are at dangerous intersections. Treat them the same way as stop signs.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Don't speed on wet roads.
Keep tires at the correct air pressure.
Replace tires with worn tread.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires glide on a layer of water. Low tire pressure, worn tread, and high speeds all increase hydroplaning risk.

questions.question: What should you do when a school bus stops with its stop arm out?

options.text: Stop completely and wait.
Honk and pass on the left side.
Drive when you think kids are done exiting.
Pass before the door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and wait.
questions.explanation: You must stop completely when a school bus has its stop arm out. Wait until the stop arm is pulled back before you drive.

questions.question: What do downward-pointing triangle signs mean?

options.text: School zones ahead.
Yield to other traffic.
Construction zone.
Railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to other traffic.
questions.explanation: Downward-pointing triangle signs tell drivers to yield. You may proceed when the road is clear and it is safe.

questions.question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?

options.text: Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
Keep a steady pace.
Stay in the driver's blind spot.
Honk to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not drive in someone else's blind spot. Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.

questions.question: Compared to driving during the day, driving at night is:

options.text: Less dangerous.
No more or less dangerous.
More dangerous.
Easier on your eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous.
questions.explanation: Driving at night is more dangerous than driving during the day. It is harder to see in the dark. Other vehicles' lights can blind you. More tired or impaired drivers may be on the road.

questions.question: When passing other vehicles, what should you do?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn at least three times.
Move back into your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.
There is no need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before passing another vehicle, check your mirrors and blind spots. Use your turn signal before changing lanes. Move back into your lane when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: What should you be most concerned about when you see this sign?

options.text: Your headlights being out of alignment because one side of your car is higher than the other.
Damaging a tire from drifting onto the shoulder.
Hydroplaning if the shoulder has water on it.
Losing control of your vehicle if you drift onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Losing control of your vehicle if you drift onto the shoulder.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the shoulder is lower than the road. If one wheel drops onto the low shoulder, do not slam on the brakes or steer sharply. This can cause you to lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is not true?

options.text: Winter is the most difficult driving season.
Check your vehicle's antifreeze and windshield washer fluid levels in winter.
Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
Snow tires are best for winter driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or similar hazardous conditions. Winter is the most difficult driving season. Check antifreeze and windshield washer fluid levels. Snow tires increase traction on slippery roads.

questions.question: Driving while under the influence of marijuana is:

options.text: Legal.
Illegal.
Legal, but not recommended.
Recommended.

questions.correctAnswerText: Illegal.
questions.explanation: Driving while under the influence of marijuana is illegal, even if you use it legally. It can distort your perception of space, time, and speed, making driving dangerous.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Signal a lane change.
Check your rearview and outside mirrors.
Check your blind spot by glancing over your shoulder.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always signal your lane change in advance. Check your mirrors. Check your blind spot by glancing over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

questions.question: You are driving at night and another vehicle is approaching from the opposite direction. Your headlights should:

options.text: Be on their high beam setting.
Be on their low beam setting.
Be off and use your parking lights instead.
Be on either their high or low beam setting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be on their low beam setting.
questions.explanation: Do not use high beam headlights when approaching or following another vehicle at night. Switch to low beam to keep everyone safe.

questions.question: Stopping completely at an intersection, yielding to cross traffic and pedestrians, then proceeding when clear matches:

options.text: A solid red light.
A flashing yellow light.
A solid green light.
A flashing red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, yield to cross traffic and pedestrians, and then proceed when the way is clear.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should use your:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
Hazard flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights and fog lights in foggy conditions. High beams bounce off fog and reduce your visibility even more.

questions.question: What should you do to turn right at a red light?

options.text: Slow down and look for traffic before turning.
Stop, signal, then turn when it is safe. Do not turn if a sign says not to.
Signal and wait until the light turns green.
Wait for a green turn arrow before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, signal, then turn when it is safe. Do not turn if a sign says not to.
questions.explanation: At a red light, you may turn right if no sign forbids it. You must stop completely first. Always signal before you turn.

questions.question: How should you prepare for hazards ahead?

options.text: Look at the entire road and both sides.
Look straight ahead at all times.
Keep your left foot lightly on the brake pedal.
Focus on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the entire road and both sides.
questions.explanation: Good driving depends on spotting problems early. Look far ahead and scan the whole road, including the sides. Do not just stare straight ahead.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in fog?

options.text: Parking lights.
Low beams.
High beams.
It does not matter which lights you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A left curve is ahead.
Curves are ahead.
An S-curve is ahead.
The road is slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road becomes slippery when it is wet.

questions.question: How can you help prevent crashes?

options.text: Tell other drivers what you are doing.
Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets.
Avoid driving during rush hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell other drivers what you are doing.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do things others do not expect. Communicate by using your turn signal, brake lights, and horn when needed. This helps other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians know what you are going to do.
